blocks.text: 1. Web Crawling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708355-644438441.png

Data sources, covered generally in Document Ingestion, described the general categories of raw content a RAG system can ingest. Web Crawling, automatically collecting pages from across a website or the wider web, gives one specific technique its own dedicated depth.
It is one specific, common way of feeding raw content into a RAG system's own ingestion pipeline.
2. Recapping Data Sources
Document Ingestion described the general categories of raw content a RAG system can ingest.
Web crawling is one specific, concrete technique for collecting one of those source types, and that narrowed focus is what this topic explores.
3. What A Crawler Does
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708355-689333060.png
A crawler starts from one or more seed pages and follows their own links outward.
It visits each newly discovered page and repeats that same process again, and that is the core mechanism this topic explores.

blocks.text: 4. Respecting Robots.txt And Rate Limits
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708356-994609348.png
Responsible crawling respects a site's own robots.txt rules about what may be crawled.
This is covered generally as rate limiting in Production RAG, a later dedicated module in this course, and it is an important ethical and practical constraint on any crawler.
5. Extracting Content From HTML
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708356-150429358.png
Raw HTML contains navigation, ads, and layout markup mixed in with the real content.
A crawler needs to extract just the meaningful text, discarding that surrounding clutter, which is the core extraction challenge here.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This extraction step connects to data cleaning, covered as a later topic in Document Ingestion, which refines that extracted content even further before it gets chunked and embedded.

blocks.text: 6. Handling Duplicate And Near-Duplicate Pages
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708357-864071848.png
The exact same content often appears at multiple different URLs across a site.
This is covered generally as deduplication in Document Ingestion, a later topic in this module, and it is a real, common crawling challenge.
7. Incremental Versus Full Recrawls
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708357-683435361.png
Re-crawling an entire large site from scratch every time wastes considerable time and bandwidth.
This is covered generally as incremental ingestion in Document Ingestion, a later topic in this module, and it is a practical efficiency concern for any crawler.

blocks.text: 8. Crawling Dynamic JavaScript Pages
Modern pages often render their own real content only after JavaScript runs.
A simple crawler fetching raw HTML alone can miss that dynamically loaded content entirely, a real, technical limitation to plan around.
9. Recognizing When Web Crawling Is The Right Ingestion Approach

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Web Crawling Is The Right Ingestion Approach
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708358-411901844.png
Web crawling suits large, link-connected sites without a direct data feed.
Direct database or API ingestion, covered generally in Document Ingestion, remains preferable when structured access already exists.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates a simplified crawler following links outward from a seed page.

code.content:
site_graph = {
    "home": ["about", "products"],
    "about": ["team"],
    "products": ["product-a", "product-b"],
    "team": [],
    "product-a": [],
    "product-b": [],
}

def crawl(seed_page, site_graph):
    visited = set()
    to_visit = [seed_page]

    while to_visit:
        current_page = to_visit.pop(0)
        if current_page in visited:
            continue  # skip pages already visited
        visited.add(current_page)
        print(f"Visiting: {current_page}")

        for linked_page in site_graph.get(current_page, []):
            if linked_page not in visited:
                to_visit.append(linked_page)

    return visited

print("Crawling starting from seed page 'home':\n")
crawled_pages = crawl("home", site_graph)
print(f"\nTotal pages crawled: {len(crawled_pages)}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the crawler starting from one seed page and discovering every reachable page by following links outward.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Ignoring robots.txt rules and crawling pages a site owner explicitly disallowed.
Crawling too aggressively without rate limits, overwhelming the target site's own servers.
Extracting raw HTML directly into the document collection without stripping navigation and ads.
Assuming a simple HTML fetch captures content that only appears after JavaScript renders.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Web crawling automatically collects pages from across a website or the wider web.
It is one specific technique for collecting one of the general data source types.
A crawler starts from seed pages and follows links outward, visiting each new page discovered.
Responsible crawling respects robots.txt rules and applies sensible rate limits.
Crawlers need to extract meaningful text from HTML, discarding navigation and layout clutter.
The same content often appears at multiple URLs, requiring deduplication.
Incremental recrawls avoid wasting time and bandwidth on unchanged pages.
Modern JavaScript-rendered pages can require more than a simple raw HTML fetch to capture fully.
